Good web design in McDonough, GA has to work for a town with two faces. One is the historic courthouse square, laid out when the city was chartered in December 1823 as the seat of Henry County and named for Thomas Macdonough, the American naval commander who beat the British fleet on Lake Champlain in the War of 1812. The other is the interstate: three I-75 exits within a few miles, lined with shopping centers, distribution buildings and the traffic of a county that grew from about 204,000 people in 2010 to more than 240,000 by the 2020 census.

Dominion Web Design Pro builds a McDonough website for either face, or both. Maurice Johnson writes every page by hand for your business, you see a free demo before you pay, and the price is printed: $497, $997 or $1,997, one time. We are based in East Texas and work with Henry County owners by phone and link.

Web design in McDonough, GA starts on the square

The blocks around the Henry County Courthouse, a building from 1897 that is listed on the National Register of Historic Places, still hold the kind of businesses a courthouse town always collects: law offices, title and insurance agents, cafes, salons, boutiques and the lunch places that fill up when court is in session. Each May the square and the surrounding streets fill for the Geranium Festival, an arts and crafts show with more than 400 booth spaces. It started in 1977 as the Henry County Chamber Arts and Crafts Festival, was taken over by the McDonough Lions Club soon after, and sends its booth money to Henry County charities and to help the visually impaired. The festival's own site counts 2026 as its 49th year.

A festival weekend is the clearest test of a downtown website. Thousands of visitors walk past your door, and some of them look you up later that evening on a phone. If your site shows last year's hours, a menu as a blurry photo or no map at all, that second visit never happens. The square rewards businesses whose pages answer three questions fast: what you sell, when you are open and where to park.

Three exits, three different customers

Most of McDonough's newer commerce sits along I-75. Each exit pulls a different kind of search, and a site written for one of them can miss the others.

Exit 221, Jonesboro Road

The interchange next to Henry Town Center and the road west toward Lovejoy. Henry County plans to widen Jonesboro Road between I-75 and North Mount Carmel Road to four lanes with transportation sales tax money, and road work changes how drivers get in. Restaurants and service shops along it need current directions on their sites.

Exit 218, Highway 20 and 81

The corridor toward Hampton, with retail on SR 20 and industrial parkways running beside the interstate. Auto service, quick lunch spots and suppliers here are chosen in a hurry, often from a map result.

Exit 216, Highway 155

Where the I-75 South Metro Express Lanes begin. Commuters heading north toward Atlanta pass it every morning, so businesses near it are found by people searching on the move.

The logistics side of the county keeps growing too. Highline Warren announced a $170 million distribution center at 830 Highway 42 South, in a 1.1 million square foot building, with about 160 jobs and operations expected to start in late 2026. Every new warehouse brings shift workers who need lunch, childcare, car repair, barbers and apartments, and most of them find those by searching from the parking lot.

Henry County homeowners hire from their phones

The subdivisions that have filled in around McDonough as the county grew created steady work for HVAC companies, plumbers, roofers, pressure washers, landscapers, house cleaners and pest control. Georgia summers are long, and an air conditioner that quits in July is an emergency. The homeowner searches, opens two or three sites, and calls whichever one makes it obvious that the company serves their part of the county and will pick up.

For a trade, that means a page for each service you want to sell, a plain list of the towns you cover (McDonough, Stockbridge, Hampton, Locust Grove or wherever you actually drive), photos of your own finished jobs, and a tap-to-call button that never scrolls out of reach. If you want calls answered after hours, the AI phone agent on the Agency package can take them, which we explain below without hiding the monthly fee.

Small business help in Henry County

  • Henry County Chamber of CommerceAt 1709 Highway 20 West in McDonough. Its Business Resource Center focuses on helping small businesses grow, especially minority- and women-owned firms, and it has run small business roundtables to shape an entrepreneur network for 2026.
  • UGA Small Business Development CenterSBDC consultants have held free drop-in advising sessions at the chamber's Business Resource Center. Check the chamber calendar for the current schedule before you go.
  • City of McDonoughThe city's tourism and downtown programs, along with events like the Geranium Festival, bring people to the square who later look businesses up online.

None of those organizations will build your website, but a free SBDC session is a smart place to test your business plan before you spend money on marketing of any kind.

Common questions

How much does a website cost in McDonough, GA?

Quotes in the south metro run from a few hundred dollars to many thousands. Dominion Web Design Pro prints its prices: Starter is $497, Pro is $997 and Agency is $1,997, each paid one time. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included while you keep the AI agent. You can see a free demo of your site before choosing any of them.

Do you do web design in Henry County outside McDonough, like Stockbridge, Hampton or Locust Grove?

Yes. The work is done remotely, so any Henry County address is the same to us. If you serve several of those towns, the Pro package includes ten city pages, and each one is researched and written for its own town instead of copied from the McDonough page.

Can a small business on the McDonough square compete with the big stores by the interstate?

Online, often yes. The chains by Exit 218 and Exit 221 win on price and parking. A shop or restaurant on the square wins on being specific: what you sell, who makes it, when you are open and what is happening downtown this weekend. A website that says those things clearly, with current hours and a map, gives a searcher a reason to drive past the big lots and park on the square.

What should a contractor serving Henry County subdivisions put on a website?

A page for each main service, the towns and parts of the county you actually cover, photos of your own finished work, your license information where Georgia requires it for your trade, and a short form that asks for the address and the problem. Homeowners usually compare two or three companies on their phones before calling one.

Is Dominion Web Design Pro located in McDonough?

No. The business is in Big Sandy, Texas, and builds every site remotely. You review the free demo and each page by link, reach Maurice through our phone line, where an AI receptionist answers any hour and can put you through to him, and approve everything before it goes live.
